implementation_notes: The copy module is the prototype mechanism: copy.deepcopy(x) recursively duplicates the object graph, keeps a memo of already-copied objects so cycles and shared references survive as shared references, and honours __deepcopy__/__copy__ when a class must control what is copied (share an immutable config, or refuse to copy a file handle). copy.copy() is the shallow variant for configured objects whose nested values are never mutated, and dataclasses.replace is the copy-with-overrides idiom for values. Immutable data (tuples, frozen dataclasses) needs no clone at all.
pitfalls: copy.copy() is shallow: nested lists and dicts are shared with the prototype, so mutating them through the clone mutates the template.
deepcopy copies everything reachable, including sockets, files and locks (they either raise or produce nonsense) - implement __deepcopy__ to share or re-create such state.
A custom __deepcopy__ must pass the memo down to nested copies and return without recursing into itself, otherwise shared references are duplicated or recursion never terminates.
